title: Battle Binder: Platform Constraints & Sales Tactics (Sketch)
body:
Slide 1 — Cover: Battle Binder: Platform Constraints & Sales Tactics (Sketch)
- One-line: Practical rebuttals and tradeoff scripts for platform/infra objections during sales cycles
- Speaker note: Quick intro: why this exists — we win or lose enterprise deals when platform constraints are misunderstood. This binder is a fast-reference for AE/SEs.

Slide 2 — Goal & Audience
- Goal: Give sellers concise, technical-safe talking points and a short decision tree to handle constraint-driven pushback (latency SLAs, capacity, VPC, data residency, cost ceilings).
- Audience: Solutions Engineers, AEs in mid-market/enterprise, field SEs supporting dedicated/private conversations.
- Speaker note: Emphasize pragmatic tactics vs. grand architecture debates.

Slide 3 — Quick framing: What customers mean by 'platform constraint'
- Common asks: "Can you meet 50ms p50 for 8k token generations?", "We need air-gapped private deployment with HSM", "Predictable cost under 1M tokens/day"
- Underlying customer concerns: latency, predictability, data sovereignty, burstiness, vendor lock-in.
- Seller script: "Tell me about the worst-case load pattern you expect—spikes, batch windows, and latency tail sensitivity."

Slide 4 — Persona cheat sheet (one-liners for different stakeholders)
- Platform/Infra Lead: Focus on determinism and isolation. Say: "We can provide dedicated pools with SLAs and predictable resource assignments; here's how we measure contention and pre-warm capacity."
- Security/Compliance: Focus on attestations and key control. Say: "Private control plane + KMS/HSM integrations, audit log exports, and SOC/ISO artifacts available."
- Product/PM: Focus on feature velocity and cost per API. Say: "Start hosted for iteration; when you hit consistent throughput we'll help plan Dedicated with predictable unit economics."
- Speaker note: Memorize the three top concerns per persona and avoid deep infra promises for PMs.

Slide 5 — Objection library: Latency is too low / tight SLAs
- Short rebuttal: "We have verified profiles across 60+ model+GPU combos and can route to low-latency region variants; for ultra-low p50 we recommend pinned model variants on Dedicated capacity."
- Technical backup bullets: kernel selection, sequence-length aware batching, KV cache hit-rate, cold-start pre-warm.
- Quick proof: share our internal benchmark snippet (p50/p99 for common models) and a recent customer case where we moved p99 from 800ms to 220ms via reserved NVLink pools.

Slide 6 — Objection library: Cost constraints / 'this will be expensive'
- Short rebuttal: "We optimize cost vs latency by tuning batching, cache TTLs, and quantization profiles — we can run a quick workload sample to estimate unit economics."
- Seller tactic: propose a two-week sampling pilot with usage telemetry; promise a follow-up with batching/caching recommendations and a cost delta before Dedicated commitment.
- Negotiation lever: reserved capacity discounts, burst pool caps, and a metered fallback to cheaper model variant under heavy load.

Slide 7 — Objection library: Private deployment / air-gapped requirements
- Short rebuttal: "Private control plane plus on-prem package available; we have documented install and upgrade playbooks and can integrate your KMS/HSM."
- Red flags: customer expects continuous model upgrades in air-gapped mode without a change window — call out longer ops lead time and include Professional Services.
- Quick checklist to ask customer: network topology, approval cadence, HSM vendor + certs, expected data egress policy.

Slide 8 — Objection library: Regulatory / data residency
- Short rebuttal: "We can run in-region Dedicated or Private deployments; audit logs and retention policies are configurable per customer."
- Practical note: confirm the list of regulators (e.g., financial vs. healthcare) — different evidence packages required.

Slide 9 — Routing & fallback strategy (playbook snippet)
- Decision tree (text): If latency SLO <= X and throughput <= Y -> propose Dedicated pinned pools. If bursty with low baseline -> propose Hosted + burst capacity + caching. If sensitive data -> Private + KMS. If cost is primary -> start hosted with sampling, then Recommend quantized variants.
- Speaker note: Provide simple numeric thresholds used in field (keep flexible).

Slide 10 — Pricing levers to discuss confidently
- Unit levers: batching window, per-token model variant, KV cache hit rate assumptions, reserved commit tiers.
- Contract levers: trial with sample telemetry, phased reserved capacity starts (pilot -> commit), rollback & fallback SLAs.
- Quick example: show sample math for 2M tokens/day with 10% cache = X cost hosted vs Dedicated (textualized).

Slide 11 — Demo checklist for SEs (pre-call)
- Bring: sample prompts (realistic), expected concurrency, latency SLO, data residency constraints, security contacts.
- Prep step: run local synthetic to approximate token distribution and share results in first 24hrs of pilot.

Slide 12 — Rapid rebuttal snippets (soundbites for call)
- "We won't be able to hit that SLA on shared noisy infrastructure — here's how Dedicated pins variability."
- "If you want the quickest time-to-value, start hosted. We'll hand off an upgrade plan to Dedicated when usage stabilizes."
- "We can export comprehensive audit logs daily and provide a signed attestation for your compliance team."

Slide 13 — Case example (anonymized)
- Customer: mid-market fintech, problem: unpredictable batch spikes causing p99 breaches.
- What we did: implemented prefix caching, moved critical routes to Dedicated NVLink pool, introduced canary traffic steering for model rollouts.
- Outcome: p99 reduced by ~60%, predictable cost growth and successful SOC audit.

Slide 14 — Risks to call out (honest language for credibility)
- Multitude of model variants increases operational complexity for the customer — propose managed rollouts.
- Air-gapped upgrades require maintenance windows and PS engagement.
- Overpromising single-digit p50 without capacity guarantee is a path to churn.

Slide 15 — Appendix: quick FAQ answers
- Q: "Can we get raw model weights?" A: "No — we provide model artifacts via runtime; custom model hosting is part of Private professional services."
- Q: "How do you handle large context windows?" A: "We select kernels and memory profiles; for extreme contexts we recommend a hybrid architecture (chunking + retrieval)."

Slide 16 — Next steps & owner actions
- For AE: pick top 3 upcoming deals with infra objections and run this binder pre-call.
- For SEs: run the 2-week sampling pilot template and deliver a cost/latency delta report.
- Document owner: Aisha Patel — this is a living sketch; pull requests to github:docs/sales/battle-binder.

Slide 17 — Open questions / research items
- Threshold guidance: define concrete numeric thresholds for "low latency candidate" vs "dedicated required" (action: run historical fleet telemetry to propose bins).
- PS scoping templates for air-gapped upgrades — create standard SOW drafts.

Slide 18 — Raw notes / phrases for quick copy-paste into email or slide
- "We treat latency like a contract: measured, instrumented, and fall-back aware."
- "Dedicated is insurance against noisy neighbors; we price it around predictable throughput rather than ad-hoc bursts."
- "Let's run a two-week proof of workload — we will deliver a tailored optimization plan with estimated cost delta."

Slide 19 — Back-channel resources and contact map
- Internal: product-ops Slack, infra on-call list, demo cluster access request form.
- External facing artifacts to attach: performance benchmarks, security pack, Dedicated price tiers one-pager.

Slide 20 — Closing: this is a living sketch
- Request: SEs/AE feedback after first 5 uses. Add examples that worked and ones that failed.
- Ownership and next sync: Aisha (owner) + Mark (deliverable templates) — weekly sync until v1.

End of deck (sketch).

Notes: informal language, placeholders for numbers and concrete benchmarks intentionally omitted here — we'll fill after infra benchmarking. This is intended as a fast, copy-paste friendly sales binder for live calls.
